why: EXPECTED UNCAUGHT, and it is the allocator that makes it so.  The skew is `(align8(p) - p) / 2` over a `sysdep_malloc` return, and glibc's malloc on i386 has MALLOC_ALIGNMENT = 2 * SIZE_SZ = 8 -- so `align8(p) == p` for every pointer this constructor can ever be given, the difference is zero, and zero halved and zero unhalved are the same number.  All six skews are 0 and all six aligned pointers equal their raw one in every trial, which is also why the object comparison cannot see it.  Held fixed: that the shift is THERE, which is a statement about the blob's bytes (`d1 ea`, finding 1231) and not about any value.  If this ever starts being caught, the harness allocator has stopped 8-aligning and the triples have become testable -- which is the good outcome, not a regression.
